method: Independent clean-room review of all 112 assigned files. Read this repository AGENTS.md first; did not consult old implementations, sibling archives, Git history, or prior audit conclusions. Reviewed every deploy implementation module and assigned test file, tracing public/operator entrypoints through validation, fixed identities and sudo verbs, request/receipt budgets, cgroup/UID shutdown proof, filesystem descriptors and link handling, provider credential/configuration layers, release construction/import/publication, installation/HTTPS/control-update recovery, workspace/Git/index/worktree transactions, and their fault-injection tests. Compared the root/deployment documentation and acceptance constraints with actual implementation, keeping historical validation statements separate from current-source assertions. Reviewed release scanning, source snapshot exclusions, targeted/full test admission and CI privilege/dependency boundaries. Read the complete lockfile as structured records and checked all package SHA-512 resolutions, package/snapshot correspondence and dependency edges; actual dependency_input accepted the current package/lock/workspace policy. Read all feature-evidence documents, reviewed method/group/workflow classifications, verified current capability-map source/report hashes and original Vitest report/suite counters, and checked protocol provenance counts/bundle hashes. Large declarative data was inspected through complete structural extraction and hash/counter validation, not accepted as proof of implementation behavior. Produced six bounded, relocated, nonprivileged local reproductions of the one confirmed compatibility defect, replacing OS/service calls only as documented below. No product/test/documentation/feature-evidence edits, full/domain suites, SSH, root execution, online changes, personal configuration/credential reads, paid inference or real MCP calls occurred. Snapshot was checked during review, before report creation and after creation.

findings.title: Configuration-layer rollback and forward recovery admit providers that require system-v1
findings.trigger: Select chatgpt-gateway, bedrock-runtime, or bedrock-mantle in a valid system-v1 instance, then invoke config-layer-rollback. The same transition is admitted by config-layer-recover --target candidate for a retained, unfinished legacy-target journal prepared with one of those providers.
findings.cause: ProviderStore.prepare explicitly refuses these provider kinds without system-v1, but rollback reuses the existing generation after checking only that config.toml equals native_config. apply_candidate publishes the legacy instance/unit/sudo configuration without checking the selected provider kind. validate_journal verifies structural fields and unit ownership but does not enforce provider/layer compatibility, so forward recovery reaches the same publication path.
findings.impact: The operation reports a committed legacy transition while preserving a provider explicitly unsupported in legacy mode. The published worker unit removes the instance requirements bind and the separate host configuration check, and its config-check unit is deleted. This violates the enforced provider compatibility and documented downgrade prerequisite. The experiment proves the persisted unsupported state and removal of those controls; it does not claim observed real-provider traffic, credential leakage, or a live-service failure.

reproduction.procedure: Create isolated relocated instance/config/unit/provider files under ignored .work. Call the real downgrade path. For forward recovery, interrupt the real path immediately after it writes the prepared journal, then pass that retained journal to the real recovery path with candidate=True. Inspect published instance.json and worker/config-check files. The actual journal validation and candidate unit ownership comparison run in the recovery cases.
reproduction.substitutions: Windows nonprivileged fixture substitutes service state/stop/reload, visudo execution, initial manager ownership/recovery preflights, user-layer Linux ownership inspection, and provider selection with a fixed current-generation model. Generated unit bytes, native_config, transaction snapshots/journals, legacy publication and forward recovery are real. Recovery snapshot modes are normalized to intended Linux 0644/0600/0440 because Windows reports writable regular files as 0666. No Linux permissions, systemd, native process or external provider behavior is claimed.

findings.recommendation: Enforce provider-kind/target-layer compatibility before a new downgrade creates a transaction or stops services, and enforce the same invariant before apply_candidate publishes a retained candidate during forward recovery. Preserve the ability to recover the old state. Require selection of a legacy-supported provider before downgrading, and add regressions for all three advanced kinds through both ordinary rollback and prepared-journal candidate recovery.

boundedExperimentsExecuted: Six nonprivileged configuration-layer downgrade/forward-recovery cases; all reproduced the finding.
limitations: Review completeness refers to the assigned source files. This round did not execute deployment/platform integration tests or a full test suite.

Historical feature evidence remains point-in-time evidence. Current capability-map hashes and stored report counters were independently checked; this does not reestablish past live-environment behavior on the frozen snapshot.

Prior audit-evidence conclusions were not read or reused. An initial generic checksum traversal processed referenced prior evidence as opaque bytes only; the final structured traversal explicitly excluded its 14 prior-audit references.
Hash-only reads of referenced files outside the assignment are not listed as source inspection. Other current source scopes belong to the other independent reviewers.
